newsitem.title: FRANCE: France, Spain consider humanitarian aid to Zaire.
newsitem.headline: France, Spain consider humanitarian aid to Zaire.

text.p: France and Spain are willing to contribute to a humanitarian operation to help refugees in eastern Zaire, Catherine Colonna, spokeswoman for French President Jacques Chirac, said on Monday.
Asked at a news conference during a Franco-Spanish summit whether in France's case this would involve sending soldiers to the area, she said: "it is a possibility which we are considering".

French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette, interviewed about his proposal earlier on Monday for urgent international talks on the Zaire crisis, said: "we have to create conditions of security" for refugees threatened by fighting.

"What we're proposing is that the international community -- Europe, the United States, African states -- organise so that there is a security force on the ground to guarantee peoples' safety," he said in an interview with France 2 television.
"France is willing to take part on the strict condition that there is an American, European and African participation," he said, speaking minutes after Colonna.

Earlier in Marseille, Spanish Foreign Minister Abel Matutes had said that Paris and Madrid favoured considering the creation of an international force to guarantee distribution of humanitarian aid in Zaire.
